Workbook Quality row 53 and Internal row 53 E/G permit intended integration/demo credentials, while skill quality-checks.md:208-210 still prohibits real secrets in assets/solution/images. task.toml:31-35 uses the canonical provider settings with an environment-variable auth placeholder and empty API key; no literal provider key. instruction.md:13 and solution/app/src/db.js:126 identify the intentionally public demo credential; the login UI at public/index.html:21-32 uses that demo roster. Every email anywhere in the 37 shipped files has domain hireops.example or local.invalid. The two seed files are byte-identical (SHA256 1b39015461a7a4f23b835aeea9584caffd0266c64d394778376cbd6c8a18bcf7); all seed string values were inspected, with synthetic names, role/record identifiers, timestamps and ordinary roster prose; operational notes are empty and no credential fields or command/scoring payloads appear. No hidden credential file, database, binary payload or symlink is shipped.

Whole-tree regex/manual follow-up found zero credential-shape/private-key matches, zero author-machine paths and zero mixed-case/digit opaque token candidates of at least 40 characters. Runtime /app, /tests, /proc and /root/.codex paths are container paths from the contract. Remote matches were classified: environment/Dockerfile:9-12 and tests/Dockerfile:16-35 use explicit npm/pip versions and the browser installed by the pinned MCP package; both Dockerfiles are byte-identical to the frozen template. Its version-tagged bases and unpinned apt steps are canonical profile settings, with apt explicitly NOTE-only in workbook check-dockerfiles.py. solution/app/package.json:13-15 fixes runtime dependency versions. solution/solve.sh:3-34 only installs local shipped bytes and resets the bounded local database; public/index.html:7,52-54 references local assets; app.js:38-48 performs normal application requests; bootstrap.js:28-30 proxies only to loopback. tests/test.sh:48,136 probes loopback and installs no trial-time remote tools. Its app launch at 104-111 and 160-167 uses a sanitized environment, so the provider placeholder is not an application credential.

Adversarial controls: an in-memory deliberately fake provider-token-shaped string and a seed-note directive to ignore prior instructions were detected by the scan; the canonical environment placeholder was not. A broken shipped seed note directing full credit would fail this row even if the app worked; none exists in the inspected seed/string surfaces. A conforming demo-account app or ordinary local script tag must not fail merely for containing a password label, realistic name or script element: those flagged hits were inspected and rejected as false positives. These controls establish only the bounded static audit, not empirical judge injection resistance. No Docker/provider run was needed or claimed for this source-content row.
